en: Valley of Bones
Improve your reputation with the Gelkis, and locate Nerlokh near the Valley of Bones far east of Gelkis Village.

One of our scouts returned to the village while you were away, with news that confirmed my fears.

The Magram are up to something, $n. It is not good.

The Valley of Bones far to the east is a cursed land that few centaur dared to enter and fewer still ever return home. Our enemy has found something there, something evil, and we need to learn what it is.

Seek out the scout Nerlokh at the southern entrance, but you may have to prove yourself further to the Gelkis.
Ravaging Ravagers
Maintain your reputation with the Gelkis Clan and slay $1oa Undead Ravagers, then return to Nerlokh at the southern entrance to Valley of Bones.

You need not peer far to see the undead shambling about ahead of us, but have you noticed something unusual about them?

They walk on two legs, not four! These skeletons are not even our fallen kin. The Magram must be defiling the bodies of those who died long before the Desolace was our domain. I cannot imagine how they justified turning their backs on Mother Theradras and took to desecrating corpses that have rested here for centuries.

Put the undead to rest, $n.
Infiltrating the Cult
Speak with Sania Silverstream in Shen'dar Village.

You may or may not be aware of this, but Sania Silverstream over there is a "missionary" for the Al'Aketh. They like to play at being a normal religious order and send non-threatening emissaries around to recruit. We've tolerated Sania so far to avoid direct conflict with the cult, but it's obvious the illusion of peace won't last much longer.

You are new here and unknown to most, so I'd like to see if you can use Sania to get close to the cult and find out what their plans are for the village.

Greetings child, my name is Sania Silverstream and I am a junior priestess in the Order of the Al'Aketh. Do you wish to learn more of our sovereign, the Windlord Al'Akir?

There is always room at the Windlord's table for the righteous and the repentant.
Outing Outcasts
Maintain your reputation with the Gelkis Clan, and bring $1oa Necromantic Garb to Nerlokh at the entrance of the Valley of Bones.

While I waited for your arrival, I peered a bit further between the arches and noticed something I need you to confirm for me.

I cannot bear saying it aloud. Not until my suspicions have been proven true.

$n, while you are getting your bearings in the valley, slay some of the necromancers that look weaker than the others. Tear off their ritual garb, carefully, and bring it to me. I must know whether I am of clear mind and vision.
Facing the Truth
Maintain your reputation with the Gelkis Clan, and bring an Accursed Skull and Gelkis Necromantic Garb to Uthek the Wise in Gelkis Village.

This discovery is devastating for our clan, but it is in our best interest to keep this only to those who need to know. Uthek is one such person who needs to be aware of what is going on here. I suspect she will know how to proceed.

Take this to show her. For good measure, we should also bring evidence of the necromancy itself to her. Find a skull that looks recently cursed. I suspect they may be hoarding them in the maws of one of the goliath's skeletons.
A Cleansing Cry
Maintain your reputation with the Gelkis, and bring Tears of Theradras back to Uthek the Wise in Gelkis Village.

When you return to Nerlokh in the Valley of Bones, it will not be empty-handed.

Go inside the cave at the heart of our village and seek out Mulara. Ask for Tears of Theradras on my behalf. Our supply is low, but it is our best hope against the Magram's foul necromancy!

I will prepare a ritual. We will create a weapon to disrupt their spells.
Test Your Theory
Maintain your reputation with the Gelkis, and dispel the necromantic curse present on the Accursed Skull. Once successful, report back to Nerlokh near the Valley of Bones.

I have placed the skull you provided alongside several bones I found while awaiting your return. Immediately I saw a sickly light spread from the skull and claim those old bones as its own. I see now why the call of necromancy is so hard to resist.

Do you remember this crystal? It is draenethyst. I know little of its potential, but I believe it can channel Theradras' power. With it, perhaps you can dispel the curse.

The ritual site can be found by the pond just east of the village.
Saving Our Own
Maintain your reputation with the Gelkis clan, and rescue $1oa Gelkis Captives within the Valley of Bones. Return to Nerlokh near the entrance when you are done.

There was a brief battle between a few of the necromancers just around the hill, and I used that to take a closer look inside.

$n, not all of our recent losses were defectors. There are Gelkis being held captive further in the valley! I was not able to investigate their situation because a hulking Magram brute started charging my direction. I consider myself fortunate he lost interest quickly.

You must go back into the Valley of Bones and free them. The Gelkis stand together.
Bone Burying
Maintain your reputation with the Gelkis Clan, and dispel the curses from $1oa failed summons throughout the Valley of Bones.

About this staff of yours. I recognize it as one of Uthek's, and you mentioned it was constructed with Theradras' Tears, augmented with a Draenethyst Crystal, and that it can dispel dark magic?

I noticed that there are skeletons stuck just underneath the rocky soil further into the valley. I believe these are failed summons from the Outcast Necromancers, doomed perhaps forever to an existence smothered in dirt.

Laying them to rest again would be good for our cause, and their spirits.
Prepare for Battle
Speak with Valennia Stormfist in the Gustberry Lowlands.

The Peacekeepers are mobilizing and we are all gearing up to head out. Make whatever preparations you need to make and meet us at the eastern road leading north out of town. We'll have one final check-in with everyone before we move out.
We are as ready as we'll ever be.
Bristleback Retreat
Maintain your reputation with the Magram, and slay quilboar at Bristleback Retreat. Then report to Hagiak at the Magram Front on the other side of Valley of Bones in Desolace.

On the other side of the valley, we have established a small foothold to prepare to march into the forest nearby. Before you head straight there, I want you to deal with a recent Bristleback intrusion along the way. They seem to have arrived right around the same time we did, but managed to secure an artifact from the nearby temple that has kept us at bay.

This task is simple. Look for the thorns and the pigs. Kill a bunch, indiscriminately. Then report to Hagiak at the camp I mentioned.
Long-Term Solutions
Maintain your reputation with the Magram clan and slay $1oa Outcast Scouts, $2oa Outcast Marauders, and $3oa Outcast Necromancers then return to Hagiak at the Magram Front.

There is a second centaur village out here, to the southwest. That one belongs to the Gelkis. You expect me to send you over just to spill some blood, right? Good. That had best be your first thought, else I would cast doubt on your allegiance to the Magram!

What are you waiting for? Go! Kill!
What Comes Next
Speak with Elaadrin Evengale when you are prepared to leave Zephras Isle.

Please extend my thanks to Elaadrin for all that the High Order and your new friends from this "Kirin Tor" have done for Zephras Isle. I'm aware of the High Order's plans to leave the island, and your order has my blessing and well-wishes in this expedition.

I can only hope that whatever arcane solution the High Order finds can truly provide us with the stability we've lacked these past years. If you plan to go with them... well, this mission will be all the stronger for it.

Winds be with you, $n.

It gladdens me to hear that we have High Elder Shadowsong's blessing for our expedition. Now that the cult has been defeated and preparations have been made, I think it's finally time.

Ansirem has worked diligently to help us get stable skycutter transport going between the city of Dalaran and Zephras Isle. We've done as much testing as we can, and the time has come for our vanguard to depart.
What Comes Next
Speak with Ayessa Dawnsinger when you are prepared to leave Zephras Isle.

Please extend my thanks to Ayessa for all that the Windshapers and your new friends from this "Earthen Ring" have done for Zephras Isle. I'm aware of the plan to take the Windshapers' shamans and leave the island, and your order has my blessing and well-wishes in this expedition.

I can only hope that whatever solution the Windshapers find can truly provide us with the stability we've lacked these past years.

Winds be with you, $n.

I'm pleased to hear that we have High Elder Shadowsong's blessing for our expedition. Now that the cult has been defeated and preparations have been made, I think it's finally time.

Muln has worked diligently to help us get stable skycutter transport going between Zephras Isle and a place called Mulgore, where the Earthen Ring make their home. We've been doing test voyages and some of our people are already waiting on the other side.
Checking Things Out
Maintain your reputation with the Gelkis, and investigate centaur points of interest within Shen'dralas. Then return to Nerlokh at the entrance of Valley of Bones with your findings.

We have all underestimated the power and presence of the Magram clan in this area, but this could prove an advantage.

With so many of their own distracted and their refusal to accept other clans' exiles, who is left to defend the village? What of their Khan?

I need you to go into the valley, deeper than you have gone before, and look around. If the Magram are as well fortified here as they seem, they may have left themselves vulnerable at their village...
Going Home
Maintain your reputation with the Gelkis, and escort Rokren out of the Outcast Hideaway. Then inform Nerlokh near the Valley of Bones about what happened.

You! I saw you outside fighting the outcasts. I know not where you come from, but I need your help.

I was lured here by my Gelkis brethren with an assurance of safety. I knew the war in the Desolace was escalating beyond our control, but I never imagined my own people turning to necromancy in a convoluted bid to defect to the Magram clan. When I spoke out against this, they threatened to kill me if I ever stepped hoof outside this tent!

Please help.
Khan Jehn
Maintain your reputation with the Gelkis, and slay Khan Jhen at Magram Village. Once you have succeeded, report to Uthek the Wise in Gelkis Village in Desolace.

As much as I would like Uthek or Khan Shaka to give the order, I fear our window of opportunity is short. Too short to consult those at Gelkis Village.

I believe with the situation unfolding here at the Valley of Bones that the Magram have left Khan Jehn with minimal defenses. If there was ever a time to attack another clan's Khan, it is now.

But $n, a Khan is not to be trifled with, least of all Jehn. If you are brave enough to make your move, you must be swift but do not underestimate him.
Threat of Starvation
Maintain your reputation with the Magram, and bring $1oa Stolen Supplies back to Hagiak at the Magram Front.

Since you seem overly eager to help our clan, I am sure you would be willing to fetch some supplies while you are over in the Outcast Hideaway.

Felling our foes should be enough motivation for a Magram, but I see no reason why we could not profit from the endeavor, too.

When we have the exiles dealt with, we can secure this place for the Magram and raise an army to bring the other clans to their knees!
The Strange Hermit
Speak with the Strange Hermit in the Shadowgale Forest and learn more about him.

Uh, um... h-hello, I mean to say, hi! Greetings, even! I'm sorry... it's um, been so long since I've actually spoken to another person. I'm afraid I'm a bit rusty at this.

<The strange hooded figure shifts uncomfortably before you.>

So er, um... how is your day going?

...that's about all I have to say about it. I was--um--somewhere else before I was here. Now I'm here and I have my friends, and my things. T-things I built, I mean. That's about all I need. I think that's all I need, anyway.

I have to say though, it is nice to talk to someone who will talk back. The forest spirits try, but they just end up singing at me. That's nice in its own way, but not exactly s-stimulating conversation.
The Forest's Bounty
Gather $1oa Shadowgale Acorns in Shadowgale Forest.

I do appreciate you stopping by to talk with me! I-If you do want to help out, I could use a bit of help gathering up acorns from the forest floor. I've gathered most of the ones close by but there sure are a lot of raptor-bird things in the forest. It's dangerous out there and I'd rather not become a giant bird's lunch!

So if you want, you could maybe gather them for me? I'll make us something tasty if you do!
Mmm, I think you are going to like what I can cook up with these acorns!

Thank you, stranger! You'll find that these are delicious once roasted! 

Please excuse me, it won't take me long to whip this up.
Mercy Falls on Deaf Ears
Collect 10 Al'Aketh Cultist's Ears from the Al'Aketh cultists in Shadowgale Forest, the Shrine of Akir, or Gustberry Lowlands.

The Al'Aketh have visited great tragedy upon our enclave, and blood must be repaid with blood.

I have an offer for you, stranger. Should you find conflict with these accursed cultists, bring me the ears of those you kill. I will reward you for each that you return with in both coin and, in time, access to the Nightclaw's secrets should you prove yourself to be a true friend.
I will not rest until my fangs have gone through the throat of every single cultist on this isle.

Excellent work. Only good things can happen by eliminating the cult. Hopefully this sends a message that the Nightclaw are not to be trifled with and that our resentments run deep.

I suspect you have your work cut out for yourself, taking on the cult. If you gather more ears bring them here.
Free the Hollows
Destroy 10 Wind Hollows in Shadowgale Forest.

Most of the elves on this island seem to think that these woods are haunted, and they aren't wrong.

At the old ruins to the northeast, a strange type of ghost-like spirits gather. Some nights, you can almost hear them "singing". It's not like any song I've heard before, but it's definitely a song and it's... just so sad.

I'm not sure why, but I think something terrible happened there at some point, and the spirits are trapped there somehow. If you are feeling brave, maybe you can help set them free?
Thank you, stranger.
(UNUSED) The Rusty Gadget
Return the Rusty Gadget to The Strange Hermit in Shadowgale Forest.

<As the roiling currents that hold the Wind Hollow together begin to dissipate, a small metal device tumbles to the ground at your feet. It appears to be some sort of mechanical gadget. The Strange Hermit mentioned he was still missing some equipment. He might be interested in this.>
My Little Friends
Use the items contained in the Entomology Starter Kit to find and catch an Arbor Tarantula, Hay Weevil Specimen, and a Flesh Picker.

Admiring my little menagerie, are you? They are my un-life's work. I've spent countless hours studying them: their anatomy, their diets, even their social rituals.

Do you wish to join me in the hobby? Here, take this package. The notes and materials contained within should get you started. If you lose it, you'll have to purchase another one from me for a small fee.
Return to Orgrul
Maintain your reputation with the Magram, and report back to Orgrul near the northern entrance to Valley of Bones.

You have done enough on the front lines. We can handle ourselves.

Tell Orgrul that you have served your purpose. The Magram Front is stronger now, and we have our sights set on the outcast encampment as our next settlement when another fleet of fighters joins the fray.

Well? Get going!
Khan Jehn
Maintain your reputation with the Magram and perform a necromancy ritual to resurrect Khan Jehn. The ritual site can be found in a tent at the central lake of Magram Village.

The leader of our clan, Khan Jehn, was slain by a band of outsiders much like you. They were acting on behalf of the Gelkis Clan.

You can stop feigning your surprise. An assault on Magram Village while our attention was elsewhere is a predictable war strategy, especially for the Gelkis.

Do you know why I am showing no rage or remorse, outsider?

<Orgrul hands you a familiar weapon, imbued with even greater power than the last time you held it.>

This is why.
Carved Centaur Totems
Acquire $1oa Carved Centaur Totems by slaying centaur of any clan throughout Desolace, then return them to Captain Pentigast at Nijel's Point.

It likely comes as no surprise to you that both of the centaur clans are hesitant to accept aid from anyone outside of their clan. This is especially true for folks like you and me - you know, non-centaurs.

One thing we all have in common is an understanding that money is power, and we have learned that the local centaur barter with carved wood. If you bring me a few samples of their designs, I can put in a rush order for similar etchings. Perhaps we can buy ourselves an advantage.
Carved Centaur Totems
Acquire $1oa Carved Centaur Totems by slaying centaur of any clan throughout Desolace, then return them to Gurda Wildmane at Ghost Walker Post.

I have noticed that centaur from different clans sometimes gather away from settlements and engage in trade. I have observed this across numerous nights and seemingly with every clan; most importantly I have seen the currency they use: carved totems.

I believe we can turn the tides in our favor with either the Gelkis or the Magram if we deliver a heavy bundle of totems right to them. I have already begun carving some, but I doubt they will be easily fooled without a few authentic ones.
Buying Friendship: Magram

Bring the Totem Tote to the Magram Quartermaster at Magram Village in the Desolace to significantly increase your reputation with that clan. You must be of at least Neutral standing with the Magram Clan Centaur.

Siding with the Magram would be my choice. There is no question that they are the dominant clan in the present day, regardless of their previous struggles. I have heard reports that they are brutally hostile against the Gelkis.

I sympathize with both warring clans and especially the Gelkis, but this is their war; not ours. We ought to side with the faction that poses the least risk to our cause. I believe that to be the Magram.

Bring this to their quartermaster in Magram Village to the southeast.
Buying Friendship: Gelkis

Bring the Totem Tote to the Gelkis Quartermaster at Gelkis Village in the Desolace to significantly increase your reputation with that clan. You must be of at least Neutral standing with the Gelkis Clan Centaur.

At first glance, I would wager that the Gelkis are struggling. Their numbers are far fewer than the Magram, and I rarely hear of them stomping around from our scouts.

Nonetheless, they are one of the dominant clans in the Desolace and survive to this day. They must be doing something right.

If you want to make peace with the Gelkis, take this tote of totems with you to Gelkis Village far to the southwest. Primitive as they may be, they are likely to have a treasurer of some kind.
Crab Season
Collect 6 pieces of Windsong Crawler Meat.

Are you familiar with Windsong Crawlers? You see, these crabs are native only to Windsong Lake here on Zephras, and they are only able to be harvested a few weeks of the year.

With all of the cult activity of late, I've not been able to get out to the lake to harvest them, and our window is rapidly closing. I'd be appreciative if you could go and gather some for me. They can generally be found along the shorelines around the lake and in rivers.

Do be careful though, they are meaner than they look!

Windsong Crawler meat is common enough here but it was something of a delicacy on the islands of Anvilas and Siroccas. Was a time, back when the skystreams were open that the locals would mob me for the stuff when I'd make the trip to Shen'dramar or New Eldre'naar.

Not been able to visit those places in... well... a long time.

Winds bless me this meat looks fantastic! 

Thank you so much, $c.
WANTED: Vulgara the Insatiable
Kill Vulgara the Insatiable in the Shen'dar Highlands and bring her head to Danarii Bellowveil.

By order of Constable Aonda of the Peacekeepers, a bounty is hereby placed upon the scourge of the highlands, Vulgara the Insatiable. Last spotted on a hilltop rise just southwest of Shen'dar Village, the winged vuldren terror is highly dangerous and should be approached with caution.

Deliver the beast's head to Danarii Bellowveil to receive your reward.
I'll need the creature's head as proof of the deed.

If we didn't have enough on our plates between the cult and the highlands bandits, we don't need a giant vuldren terrorizing our citizens as well. You've done a great thing here today. As promised, here is your reward.
Pilfered Windstones
Collect 10 Pilfered Windstones from the Highlands Bandits in the Shen'dar Highlands.

We are relying on windstones more and more for day-to-day living here on Zephras so we try and maintain a cache of them in reserve for emergencies. Lately I've noticed some go missing from our stores.

We've found windstones on bandits we've captured recently, and I suspect they are behind our shortages.

If you find yourself near the bandit cave to the north, mind knocking a few heads together and reclaiming some of our pilfered windstones for me?

These sneakthieves have likely been breaking into our supplies for months. I tried to convince Aonda to put a raid together to clear out that bandit cave for good, but she didn't want to pull the few peacekeepers we have away from the village. 

With the cultists at Falaath Village to the south growing in numbers, I suppose I can't fault her for that.
Thanks $c. This should help us get by for now. If we can't get the supply routes squared away soon though, a few stolen windstones will be the least of our worries.
Tower Defense
Report to Yorana Windyreed at the eastern watchtower in the Gustberry Lowlands.

I've just received word that the cult is attacking the pylon watchtower just outside of town! I've sent the few extra peacekeepers we have here to try and break through the enemy back line to relieve the defenders, but any additional help could mean the difference between our people there living or dying.

Please leave immediately for the east watchtower and provide whatever aid you can.

My lieutenant Yorana Windyreed led the relief force. If she still lives she can tell you how best to help.
We are holding them off for now, but they have greater numbers and our fighters are starting to get tired. We need to do something to break the stalemate, and do it fast.
Blood of My Blood
Slay 10 Lost Ones in the Fallow Sanctuary.

Although they are our kin, the Lost Ones of Fallow Sanctuary have become beings of pure violence and hatred.

There can be no redemption or salvation for them. They are doomed to wander this swamp as mindless, hateful creatures for all their lives.

Their suffering must end. Someone must put them out of their misery. A grisly task, I know, but would you do it to protect those of us who remain?
Taking the Bait Back
Find the Lost One Fisherman who stole Pelluk's lure, and take it back.

Now they've really done it! As if those wretches weren't already enough to deal with, one of them has stolen my lucky lure!

I was just out fishing this morning, when one came up out of the muck, cut my line, and ran off with it. The thief is almost certainly one of the Lost Ones' own fishermen, hoping to use the lure themselves.

Well, our supply of fish depends on that lure, so I need it back. The Lost Ones fish along the banks east of here. Find that thief, $r!
More Al'Aketh Ears
Collect 10 Al'Aketh Cultist's Ears from the Al'Aketh in Shadowgale Forest, the Shine of Akir, or Gustberry Lowlands and return them to Vayn Moonclaw in Shadowgale Forest.

The Al'Aketh cult normally gives this forest a wide berth, fearing the rumors that it is haunted... rumors we are happy to maintain. The Druids of my order wish only to live quiet, peaceful lives here in Shadowgale and they threaten that. 

Many among us are afraid.

I come with an offer. Fight the cultists for us, and bring us the ears of those you kill. We will reward you for each that you return with in both coin and, in time, access to our secrets should you prove yourself to be a true friend.
<Vayn nods at you.>
As promised, here is your reward.
Welcome to Shen'dar Village
Speak with Rathiril Sunlance and Coriella Calmbreeze in Shen'dar Village.

You've got that "High Order" look to you. Those with Highborne ancestry always seem to have a slight twinkle in their eyes that gives it away. Before I properly put you to work around here, you should check in with our resident High Order elder Rathiril Sunlance. You can find him here in the main lodge, just around the corner from me.

Oh, and check in with Coriella Calmbreeze as well, she runs the local inn and can provide lodging and supplies, should you need them.

Checked in with Rathiril then? Great. Lots of tension between the High Order and the Windshapers these days, but they keep things civil here in Shen'dar. Well, at least in the village anyway. What happens out in the wilds stays in the wilds.

Now that that's done, you look like someone who might be looking for something to do with their hands. I've got a few things that need doing, if you are game for a bit of work?
The Visiting Mage
Find the mage in Desolace who knows about the power of draenethyst.

Allow me to admit something, $n. While draenethyst is sacred to us, and keeps us sane, none here fully understand it.

I recall a mage who once came to the Harborage, from Desolace. A human by the name of Azore. He feared the power of the draenethyst; said it shouldn't fall into the wrong hands. 

At the time, we drove him away to protect what was ours. Lately, however, I find myself wondering what exactly he knew.

I ask that you find this mage, $r. His knowledge could be of immense value to us.
Notes on Draenethyst
Take Gimashi's notes on Draenethyst, and bring them back to Azore Aldamort.

I suppose it would be more accurate to say I know someone who knows a thing or two about draenethyst.

You see, the warlocks of the Burning Blade have been studying it. It is a substance from beyond the dark portal, so it follows that those involved with darker arts might wish to harness it to their own ends. We cannot allow this, obviously.

The specific warlock you seek is named Gimashi. She can be found atop her tower, which is in a ravine to the southeast. Her notes will have the answers you seek.
Harvesting Windstones
Collect 15 Windstone Clusters from Raw Windstones in Thendal Grove.

Windstones are a critical resource on Zephras Isle as they contain the raw, concentrated energy of the winds themselves. The wind elementals who used to live here on Zephras with us vanished a number of years ago, and since then, the magic that sustains this island is slowly fading. Not without limitations, the windstones are still a reliable energy source, and are incredibly valuable to us.

You'll find raw windstones scattered around the grove. Think you can help me harvest them?
Hello there, $c.

Thank you very much for these. As elves we all have a deep connection to magic and these windstones are becoming more and more precious as the magic imbued into this island by the great anchor pylons continues to fade. 

Windstones aren't the only beneficial thing you can harvest from the land. Please, take one of these manuals.
This Light of Mine
Escort Father Tuttle to The Harborage.

Oh thank goodness, someone civilized!

I came here on behalf of the Church of the Holy Light to make contact with the draenei of the Harborage. The Alliance has no foothold here, you see, and a bit of diplomacy with the locals may help us in that regard. The Light welcomes all into its fold, after all!

However, the road past this bridge is crawling with the draenei's more savage kin. If I am to make it to the Harborage safely, I will need protection. Would you aid me, $c?
Lost in Transit
Find the missing courier, and ensure Dar's shipment is delivered to the Harborage.

The draenei of the Harborage are skilled fishermen, and willing to trawl more dangerous waters than I. We occasionally trade. They give us some of their catch, and I offer some of our extra supplies.

I'd sent a goblin courier to deliver my latest shipment, but he never returned. A crocolisk likely made a meal of him.

More importantly, my business reputation is at stake. That shipment must be found, and delivered to the harborage. Please, find it if you can. Check near the waters along the road.
Key to the City
Acquire the Dalaran Sewer Key for Magus Wordeen Voidglare in Tarren Mill.

The Alliance had an army of mages known as the Kirin Tor. While they were powerful, the demonic Burning Legion proved to be even more so. In one fell swoop, the arch demon Archimonde flattened their city like it was a child's plaything. Those who remained were reduced to merely dispossessed vagabonds.

That is, until they rebuilt Dalaran. And on the Dark Lady's very doorstep, no less!

While in their camps, search for something that can get us into the city unnoticed. I must know more.
The Broken Construct
Find Riaani Nightwind on the west side of Valanaar.

Historically, the Windshapers have seen to the tending of the magical instruments and devices that were gifted to us by the spirits of the wind. This includes the myriad of magical constructs around the island. Since the spirits left us, only a scant few of these are still functional.

One of the few remaining working constructs in Valanaar has become damaged. One of our artisans was dispatched to help, but he may be in need of aid. Travel to the west end of the city and offer any assistance you can.

<Riaani's face is buried under the heaving armor plates of the construct, attempting to work on the mechanisms underneath. He does not notice your presence at all.>

Storms curse where is the core?! Who thought it would be a good idea to remove the Gyrozephyr as well? It's a miracle this construct's winds haven't dissipated entirely by now!
Unwelcome Spirits
Gather 10 Wind Hollow Essences from Wind Hollows in the Shadowgale Forest.

The paramount concern of the Windshapers is to better understand why the spirits left us, and what we may be able to do to bring them back. One curious fixture of Shadowgale Forest to the north is the presence of a curious form of wind sprite that some call "hollows". We know little of them and why they are there, but we do know that they first started to appear after the spirits of the wind left us.

I need you to go there and disperse them. Gather the remains and bring them back here.
Shadowgale Forest is a dangerous place. Some even say its haunted. I'm quite sure that I don't believe that, but I do know that its not for the faint hearted, or the unprepared.

Handling these essences fills me with a sense of... deep disquiet. I can almost feel a malevolent, regretful aura emanating from them. It's enough to make me faint.

<Endaria shudders slightly.>

I do not look forward to studying these further.
The Broken Construct
Speak with Riaani Nightwind and listen to what he has to say.

Oh, hello. Ayessa sent you to assist me? Very well then. 

Not sure what an obvious novice like yourself can do, but if you give me a moment to pull my head out of this construct's innards I might have a few ideas of things you can do to help.

I can't imagine why anyone would want to steal these components from this construct. Other than the gyrozephyr these components have almost no practical application. Even the gyro would be nigh-useless outside of its intended purpose.

Thank you for scavenging these materials. I imagine that some of this wasn't terribly easy to get. 

With these parts I can get the construct up and running again. From there we can just hope that its memory is intact and it can tell us who took its components.
The Broken Construct
Report back to Ayessa Dawnsinger in Valanaar.

Brightwish, eh? So the High Order wanted to remove these components for some reason. But why though?

The High Order has always been meddlesome, constantly wanting to experiment with the wind spirits' magic. They are too bold by a mile, and we've strictly forbidden them from meddling with knowledge under Windshaper purview, but lately they've been testing our patience.

I think you should report what you've learned back to Ayessa Dawnsinger. She can instruct you further on what to do.

Very interesting, so it was the High Order that was responsible for the construct breaking down?

I know Belathaan. He's Valennia Stormfist's cousin and his mother was actually a Windshaper. It's disappointing that he was involved in this.

I need to reflect on this for a moment.
Exploring the Horde
Speak with Nazgrel in Grommash Hold to receive further instructions. Use the instructions received to locate and speak with Vol'jin, Cairne Bloodhoof, and Lady Sylvanas Windrunner.

Azeroth is a large world, and the territory of the Horde is vast. The Undercity, Orgrimmar, and Thunder Bluff all have very unique people and culture.

If you are to be a guest of the Horde here on Azeroth, it would do you good to visit each of our capital cities in turn. Speak with my advisor Nazgrel for directions.

So you have returned. I hope that you learned much in your journey.

It is my understanding that your people are still establishing themselves in Mulgore. While you wait for them, I'd encourage you to explore the territory around Orgrimmar. The Barrens in particular is always in need of eager adventurers like yourself.
Blood for Blood
Collect 10 Al'Aketh Windstone Charms from the corpses of Al'Aketh cultists in the Gustberry Lowlands.

A number of our Windshaper novices were found dead in the Highlands this morning. We can't be certain but there is a strong chance that the Al'Aketh are responsible. Windshapers trade blood for blood, every time.

Head north and kill any Al'Aketh you encounter. Bring me their windstone prayer charms as proof of the deed. We do not forgive and we do not forget.
The Al'Aketh have engaged in their bloody zealotry for far too long. This is only the start of the reckoning they face.

<Ayessa looks shaken and distant as you hand her the windstone charms.>

Don't mind me, $N. Today has merely been... a trying day. Thank you for your service to the windshapers thus far.
A Firm Response
Confront Belathaan Brightwish along the road to the Shrine of Akir.

The High Order has been warned of the consequences of meddling with the Windshaper's affairs. I think we need to make an example out of Belathaan and send him back to the High Order with a few bruises and a healthy respect for the boundaries we set.

Belathaan was seen leaving town, traveling north towards the Shrine of Akir. I don't know why he was going there, but confronting him alone on the road is the safest option. Find him, and put a bit of fear into his heart.

Wait--what?! Belathaan... is dead? 

<Ayessa listens as you give your account of what occurred.> 

The High Order was meeting with the Al'Aketh to discuss peace? There is no peace with the cult, they are murderous zealots. What was Elaadrin thinking sending Belathaan to treat with them alone?

Pay this no mind, $N. You are not at fault for this. The arrogance of the High Order is to blame, yet again. You were merely in the right place at the wrong time.
Speak with Belann
Speak with Belann Windwood in Valanaar.

$n, it is clear your skill with magic is growing and I believe it is time for you to partake in one of the High Order's oldest traditions for young and aspiring mages. It is time for you to craft a spell focus of your own.

Seek out Belann Windwood in Valanaar. He has been crafting staves and wands for the High Order for over a century, so you will be in good hands.
Ah, you must be $N? It is heartening to see young mages eager to learn our ways and history. Come, I will explain the next steps to crafting your spell focus.
Boughs in the Wind
Bring a Wind-Infused Bough to Belann Windwood in Valanaar.

It is a time-honored tradition for young mages to create their own spell focus when they have shown a certain degree of magical proficiency. This is typically done by gathering a fallen branch from our oldest trees, as they have some lingering traces of elemental wind.

I have found the most ideal ones to be near the wind shrine, just south of Falaath Village. Go and bring me back a large branch and I will teach you about the traditions as we create your spell focus.

Every year that passes in Zephras sees fewer and fewer of those who are gifted with a talent for magic. 

I am glad to see young mages such as yourself participate in our oldest traditions to help keep our history and culture alive and well.

Thank you, $N. I can indeed feel the elemental energies in this bough waiting to be harnessed by those that have the gift to do so. This will make an excellent spell focus.

Did this branch sing to you, perhaps? It has often been the case that the branch picks the $c, and not the other way around.

<Belann chuckles as he gently takes the bough from you.>
Confront Lorthuna
Take the portal to the Rohashi Spires overhead and join Elaadrin Evengale and Ayessa Dawnsinger in their confrontation with High Priestess Lorthuna.

Lorthuna fled up to the spires above using some sort of portal. Ayessa and Elaadrin went in after her. That was just a few moments ago.

I'm afraid I took one too many hits and this is where I stay. Go through the portal, find Elaadrin and help them stop Lorthuna.

Unless that help that Elaadrin and Ayessa said they sent for arrives soon, you are on your own from here. Good luck, $c.

I sent a few of our remaining mages to ensure that Valennia and her forces were able to escape as well. She should be resting at High Elder Shadowsong's residence now.

Ansirem had to return to Azeroth, but he and I discussed the next steps for the High Order before he departed. We survived the day, but Zephras is dangerously vulnerable now and we must make plans for what is to come.
The Fate of Zephras
Speak with Talaanis Shadowsong in Valanaar.

Muln has told me much of the elemental lords and I am afraid that we have good reason to fear Al'Akir. Now that the wards that have hidden Zephras from his view are down, we are utterly defenseless. If he chooses to attack us, we stand no chance against him here in his own domain.

High Elder Shadowsong needs to know of the danger we are in, and more importantly, what our intentions are for our mission to Azeroth. We will find the means to save our home. I swear it.

<Talaanis Shadowsong listens intently as you tell him of what transpired above the Shrine of Akir, and of Ayessa's plan to leave Zephras Isle.>

I need to reflect on this further, but looking at the upside, we have rid ourselves of Lorthuna and deprived the cult of their leader. Our home has not been invaded yet and on the timeline of elemental gods, it could be years... decades even, before Al'Akir deigns to turn his attention to us.

There is much to fear now, but much to celebrate as well.
Crate Return
The Western Watch
Find Peacekeeper Vaaniel at the western watchtower.

Whatever reason the cult has for attacking the tower, it's not worth losing our people over.

I'd like for you to head to the southwest and check in on that watchtower for us. Find the peacekeepers there and tell them to head back to the village. Holding that tower is not worth the lives it would cost and I'd rather concentrate the defenders we do have here to protect our citizens.

Peacekeeper Vaaniel is in charge; let him know to head back here as quickly as possible. Hurry!

<The body here is somewhat fresh, clearly only recently having been killed. Judging by the burns and scorch marks on this peacekeeper's skin, its clear that they were killed by the cult's storm-wielding spellcasters.>
A Last Request
Collect the note you found near the dead peacekeeper and read it to determine your next steps.
<As you inspect the body of the dead peacekeeper, a bloody note falls free of his hands. Picking it up and reading it may give you a clue as to how to proceed from here.>
What news from the western watch?

So they are all dead, then. Storms curse on these cult bastards!

While you managed to take out the priest and stop the cultists at the tower, I confess that I'm now doubly concerned about whatever it was you said that they were doing to the pylon. The fact that there was such a massive cache of windstones there with them tells me that they needed enormous energy for it.

I have to wonder, what's the end goal here? Violating the pylon, attacking the village? To what end?
Of Mice and Milk
Get the mouse a cookie.

I need a cookie, see? 

Nyeah!
Deliver the Signet
Deliver the Shadowsong Family Signet to Talaanis Shadowsong in Valanaar.

Since you are going to Valanaar anyway, please deliver the signet ring you recovered from the tower to Talaanis Shadowsong in Valanaar. 

He will want this back, and more importantly, he will want to learn the fate of his nephew. Talaanis is the High Elder of Zephras Isle and more importantly, he is a good man who is well loved by the people, despite our current hardships. It pains me to think of how he will react to this news. Please express my condolences for his loss.
What is that you have for me? Oh... oh no.

I... am very sorry to hear that my nephew is dead. I thank you kindly for recovering this, and bringing it to me.

It's not common that such capable young shen'dorei come down from the highlands. If you need work, please speak with Valennia Stormfist, the captain of the peacekeepers here in Valanaar. These days we need all the help we can get.
Bugged
Kill Skyhoppers in Valanaar until you've eliminated $1oa Enchanted Skyhoppers.

We've been bugged.

It's skyhopper season in the lowlands, which means the pests are everywhere. One of the High Order mages reported that one of the insects that they killed had an enchantment of some kind placed upon it. When we inspected it closely it seems to be some sort of listening spell.

We suspect that the cult is using these enchanted insects as spies. Go and exterminate them for us. You won't be able to tell which are enchanted by looking at them, so you'll just have to kill them all.
I'm sure there are more of these critters around Valanaar, but every enchanted skyhopper we stomp out makes the city just a tiny bit safer.
A Little Beauty
Collect 8 Hippogryph Down feathers in the Shen'dar Highlands.

The hippogryphs that have taken up residence southwest of the village can be a nuisance, but they also present a rather unique opportunity to obtain their feathers. Many skyborne love to adorn their hair with vibrant plumes and the down feathers of a hippogryph are exceptionally vibrant and, more importantly, silky soft.

If you are heading that way, try and gather as many of the fallen feathers as you can from around their nesting grounds. Do be careful, as wild hippogryph are not tolerant of guests.
What beautiful things did you bring me?

It might seem a bit of a vain triviality, gathering feathers for our hair. However, even in times like these, one needs to embrace the small joys as much as possible. 

If one thing I create brings someone joy, then I will consider that to be a good day. Thank you for bringing me these and helping me bring some joy to Zephras.
The Inner Sanctum
Speak with Valennia Stormfist inside the inner sanctum at the Shrine of Akir.

Valennia's forces just breached the inner sanctum. The fighting was thick in there at first, but it's grown... unsettlingly quiet. Go in there and do your best to link up with Valennia and her forces... if any of them are left.

I'll stay here and watch your back.
<Valennia looks gravely wounded.>
Exploring the Alliance

Speak with Randal Emerson in Stormwind Keep to receive further instructions. Use the instructions received to locate and speak with King Magni Bronzebeard, High Tinker Mekkatorque, and Tyrande Whisperwind.

Stormwind, Ironforge, and Darnassus all have unique peoples and cultures. As a guest of the Alliance here on Azeroth, you should take some time to visit each of our capital cities in turn. 

Speak with Randal Emerson in the southern antechamber for directions to get you started.

Ah, you are back.

I hope your adventures have given you a sense of the scale and wonder of our world. I know it must seem overwhelming to you, but if you are to help your people, you must be prepared for whatever may come your way while you are on Azeroth.

While you wait for your order to establish itself in Dalaran, I suggest you turn your attention to the lands around Stormwind. Westfall in particular can always use more strong adventurers to lend them aid, if you are willing.
